match.reason: No bank point teaches personal voice at the Stage 4 (Years 7-8) depth: the closest, 'Finding a voice', is written for Year 10 and Year 12, and the others cover speaking delivery, other forms, or point of view at higher levels.

draft.title: Personal voice
card: Voice is the personality a reader hears in a piece of writing. Two writers can describe the same event and still sound quite different.
Word choice builds voice. Slang and short words sound casual and friendly. Formal, precise words sound serious and distant.
Sentence rhythm and humour also shape voice. Short, quick sentences sound energetic. Long, flowing ones sound calm or thoughtful. A joke or a playful comment can make a writer sound lively.
Tone is the writer's attitude, such as cheerful, serious or sarcastic. A strong voice feels like a real person talking, so it can keep a reader interested.
draft.remember: Voice is the personality you hear in writing, built from word choice, rhythm, humour and tone.

a.q: Which sentence has the most casual, chatty voice?
opts: Honestly, my brother's cooking is a total disaster zone
My brother's cooking is generally considered unsatisfactory
The standard of my brother's cooking is rather disappointing
My brother's cooking does not meet the expected standard
a.why: Honestly and total disaster zone are casual, playful words that sound like a person talking. The other three use formal, distant words, so they sound serious.
a.clue: Which one sounds like a friend talking?

b.q: Mia writes: "I ran. Tripped. Got up. Ran again." What does her sentence rhythm do to her voice?
opts: Makes it sound rushed and energetic
Makes it sound calm and thoughtful
Makes it sound formal and distant
Makes it sound slow and dreamy
b.why: Short, quick sentences give a fast, energetic pace, so the voice sounds rushed. Long, flowing sentences would sound calm or thoughtful, which is the opposite effect.
b.clue: Think about how quickly each short sentence ends.

a.best: Honestly, my brother's cooking is a total disaster zone

b.best: Makes it sound rushed and energetic
